chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu al-Hasan Zarif, from Aban, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

«The virgin who has a father may not be married in mut'ah except with her father's permission.» This hadith can be interpreted in several ways, one of which is that the virgin may be a young girl, for it is not permissible to have sexual pleasure with her except with the permission of her parents, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the requirement for a virgin's marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing the necessity of the father's consent for a virgin daughter's *mut'ah* marriage, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on paternal authority in marital contracts. The text further explores the interpretation that 'virgin' may refer to a pre-pubescent girl, in which case permission from both parents is required for consummation, highlighting the nuanced application of *wilayah* (guardianship) across different stages of female maturity.
